title: SQL
goal: Read related records and keep values separate from SQL syntax.
explanation: SELECT chooses columns and FROM chooses the source. WHERE filters rows. JOIN combines related tables using an explicit relationship.
Use parameterised queries for user-controlled values. Placeholder syntax depends on the database driver; do not copy one driver’s placeholders into another blindly.
An ORDER BY is needed when the result order matters. Limit the selected columns and row count to what the feature needs, and review query plans for slow queries.
code:
-- PostgreSQL-style parameterised query; bind $1 through your driver.
SELECT id, name, price
FROM products
WHERE price < $1
ORDER BY price ASC;
exercise: Write a query for products below a supplied price. Explain how the driver binds the price safely.
hint: The supplied price is a bound value, not concatenated SQL text.

quiz.question: What is the safer way to include a user-supplied value?
options: Bind it as a query parameter
quiz.explanation: Binding parameters keeps data separate from SQL syntax. Authorisation and validation are still required.
